items.stem: A cell is placed in a solution with a much higher solute concentration than its cytoplasm. What happens to the cell?

options.text: Water leaves the cell by osmosis and the cell shrinks
options.rationale: Correct: water moves toward the higher-solute (hypertonic) side, so the cell loses water.

options.text: Water enters the cell and it swells and may burst
options.rationale: That describes hypotonic surroundings, the opposite case.

options.text: Nothing, because membranes block all water movement
options.rationale: Water crosses membranes readily via the bilayer and aquaporins.

options.text: Solute is actively pumped in until concentrations match
options.rationale: The immediate passive response is water loss by osmosis.

items.explanation: Correct: water moves toward the higher-solute (hypertonic) side, so the cell loses water.

items.stem: Which TWO organelles are directly involved in producing and packaging proteins for secretion? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: ribosomes on the rough ER synthesise secretory and membrane proteins.
Correct: the Golgi modifies, sorts and packages proteins for secretion.
Peroxisomes handle oxidative reactions, not secretory protein packaging.
Smooth ER handles lipid synthesis and detoxification, not protein packaging.

items.stem: During which process is the majority of ATP generated in aerobic respiration?

options.text: Oxidative phosphorylation at the inner mitochondrial membrane
options.rationale: Correct: the electron transport chain and ATP synthase produce most ATP.
Glycolysis yields only a small net amount of ATP.
The cycle mainly supplies electron carriers, not bulk ATP directly.
Fermentation regenerates NAD+ but makes little ATP.

items.explanation: Correct: the electron transport chain and ATP synthase produce most ATP.
